S37.01.needs: a signed-in account (a project already created helps, to see a list)
S37.01.note: The app calls notebooks "Projects"; the word "Notebook" does not appear in the UI. The sidebar entry can be hidden by the user (hideable: true).
steps: Sign in and click "Projects" in the left sidebar.
Look for the page heading "Projects" and the search box "Search projects...".
Each card is one project. Click a card's name ("Open project <name>") to open it.
Compare: you should see your list of projects and open one. If there are none, the text "Create one to group conversations, attach files, and share instructions." shows.
S37.01.where: Sidebar > Projects (the Projects page lists every project as cards, with the search box "Search projects...")

S37.02.note: The Projects page also has its own inline create form ("New project" in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ProjectGallery.tsx) with the placeholder "Project name"; the path above is the one the page opens.
steps: Click "Projects" in the sidebar.
Click "New project" at the top of the page.
In the dialog titled "Create project", type a name in the field "Project name" (optional: pick a template under "Start from").
Click the "Create project" button at the bottom right. Compare: the dialog closes and the new project appears in the Projects list and stays there after you reload.
S37.02.where: Sidebar > Projects > New project > Create project

S37.03.note: Project cards in Projects also have a menu with "Edit details" that opens the same settings.
steps: Create a project (see S37.02) and open it from Projects.
Fill the "Description" box in the "Create project" dialog, or later click "Project options" at the top right of the project and then "Project settings".
In "Project settings", change the "Project name" or "Description" text.
Click "Save". Compare: the new title and description show on the project page and stay after reload.
S37.03.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings

S37.04.needs: a project with at least one source file added (see S37.06)
S37.04.note: On a narrow window the same toggle may appear only inside the Panels menu.
steps: Open a project from Projects and send a first message in its composer (placeholder "New chat in <project name>").
In the chat, click the "Panels" button in the top bar.
Click the folder icon labelled "Project sources" (its tooltip; it toggles to "Close project sources").
Compare: a list of the project's sources opens beside the conversation.
S37.04.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > New chat in <project name> (send a message) > Panels > Project sources

S37.06.needs: a PDF or text file on the Mac
S37.06.note: Accepted types are images, PDF, Office files and text (packages/contracts/types/src/chat.ts). Indexing for chats is server work and is not visible as its own screen.
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources" (or "+ Add sources" when files already exist).
Click "Upload" ("Files from your device") and choose a PDF or text file from the Mac file picker.
Compare: an "Uploading" banner shows the progress, then the file appears in the source list.
S37.06.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Upload

S37.10.note: Connectors are set to coming_soon (CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE in packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts). The picker needs GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY and GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID, which the owner has not set, so the Expected cannot be met yet.
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources", then look at the "Google Drive" card.
Compare: the card is disabled and shows "Coming soon", so a Drive file cannot be picked in this build.
S37.10.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Google Drive (shows Coming soon)

S37.11.note: If no title is typed, the source is named "Text note" (AddSourcesModal.tsx). Notes in the Notes section are a separate feature.
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources", then "Text input" ("Paste or type text").
Optionally type a title in "Title (optional)", then paste or type text in the large box.
Click "Add text". Compare: a new source with that title appears in the Sources list.
S37.11.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Add sources > Text input

S37.14.needs: a project with a source file added
S37.14.note: Grounding happens on the server; the answer quality is not checked by this step.
steps: Open a project that has at least one source file added (see S37.06).
Click the composer box with the placeholder "New chat in <project name>" and type a question about the file's content.
Send it and wait for the answer.
Compare: the answer uses the project's sources and points to them (citation chips such as "p. 2" appear in the answer).
S37.14.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > composer "New chat in <project name>"

S37.15.note: A checkbox in the same dialog, labelled "Use your profile and instructions for AGI", controls whether account instructions also apply.
steps: Open a project and click "Project options" at the top right.
Click "Project settings", then type in the "Instructions" box (for example: answer in one sentence).
Click "Save".
Open a new chat in the project and ask a question. Compare: the reply follows the instruction.
S37.15.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Project options > Project settings > Instructions

S37.19.needs: a project with a PDF source and a question that uses it
S37.19.note: The chip is a link built from the citation (packages/contracts/types/src/project-file-citations.ts); a page location appears only when the citation has one.
steps: In a project chat that has sources, ask a question whose answer comes from a file.
Look for the citation chip under the answer, showing the file name and a place such as "p. 2".
Click the chip.
Compare: the project's Sources tab opens with a preview of that file at the cited page.
S37.19.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > ask a question in a project chat > click the citation chip under the answer

S37.23.note: The button opens a chat with a prompt; the briefing is a chat reply, not a saved file. The label is "Briefing doc", not "Briefing document".
steps: Open a project with a source file and click the "Sources" tab.
Under "Create from your sources", click "Briefing doc".
Compare: a new chat in this project opens and starts writing a briefing from the sources.
S37.23.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Briefing doc

S37.24.note: Opens a new chat; the guide appears as the chat reply.
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Study guide" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a study guide (quiz, essay questions, glossary) from the sources.
S37.24.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Study guide

S37.25.note: The button is labelled "FAQ", not "Frequently asked questions".
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "FAQ" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a list of questions and answers from the sources.
S37.25.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > FAQ

S37.26.note: Opens a new chat; the diagram is shown as the chat reply.
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Timeline" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and writes a dated timeline (as a Mermaid diagram plus a list) from the sources.
S37.26.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Timeline

S37.27.note: Opens a new chat; the map is a Mermaid mindmap in the reply.
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Mind map" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and draws a mind map of the sources' topics.
S37.27.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Mind map

S37.28.note: Opens a new chat; the table is a chat reply.
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Data table" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens and returns a markdown table of facts from the sources.
S37.28.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Data table

S37.30.note: The request sets officeCreationEnabled, so the result is meant to be a .pptx file; whether it is produced is not checked here.
steps: Open a project with source files and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Slide deck" under "Create from your sources".
Compare: a new chat opens with a request for a PowerPoint file built from the sources.
S37.30.where: Sidebar > Projects > open a project > Sources tab > Create from your sources > Slide deck

labels.text: Everyone in the workspace can view

S37.34.needs: a team workspace with a second member account in it
S37.34.note: The plan marks this as unfinished in the UI. Sharing is also on the project page under Project options > Share.
steps: Click "Projects" in the sidebar, then open the menu on a project card ("Project options").
Click "Share". The dialog titled "Share <project name>" opens.
Choose "Everyone in the workspace can view" or "Only people you invite", then click "Share".
Compare: the access list shows "Can view" or "Can edit" for members. On a personal account the dialog only says "Only you can open this project. Switch to a team workspace to share it."
S37.34.where: Sidebar > Projects > project card menu > Share > Share <project name>

S37.37.needs: a project with a source file
S37.37.note: The plan marks this as unfinished in the UI. On plans with AGI Work the same button is labelled "Project or folder" (ChatComposerNew.tsx).
steps: On the main chat screen, click the "Project" button in the composer's bottom bar.
Type part of a project name in "Search projects..." and click the project.
Type a question about that project's content and send it.
Compare: the reply uses that project's sources and instructions, and the chat is shown as part of that project.
S37.37.where: New chat (main chat) > the "Project" button in the composer > pick a project in "Search projects..."

S37.38.needs: a second app or browser signed in to the same account
S37.38.note: Sync is server-side (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts); the Desktop app shows the hosted web app, so this is the same screen on both.
steps: On the Desktop app, open "Projects" and note a project name, its sources and its notes.
Sign in to the web app with the same account and click "Projects".
Compare: the same project, with the same sources, appears there.
S37.38.where: No control of its own; visible by signing in to a second app with the same account and comparing the Projects list
